decisions.statement: A verdict is kept beside the page of the service the verdict is about.
A verdict never reaches the commit.
A verdict is no better than the moment of the look that left that verdict.
One look leaves one moment on the page of the service that did the looking.
A moment says a run looked rather than saying anything about one service.
A verdict is written only where the look's finding differs from the verdict published.
The verdict already there is read from the value published rather than from a ledger.
A value cleared away differs from a look's finding.
The first look after a service is installed writes that service's verdict.
The moment is written after every verdict.
A look finding its own page nowhere leaves no moment rather than leaving a moment.
A service no look reached carries no verdict rather than a verdict saying broken.
A verdict replaces the verdict written before.
The key a verdict is under and the key a moment is under are named here alone.
Nothing here decides whether a service is well.
Whether a reading is current is read off its taker's verdict and the moment of the look.

definition: what a look at the health of every service leaves published
